items.title: Dick Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006
items.q: Television didn’t appear in my life until 1952 around the time of the Eisenhower election.

ctx.x: Was it a big part of your hearing music when you grew up?

Yes it was. Remember, it was before television. Television didn’t appear in my life until 1952 around the time of the Eisenhower election. And we got a T.V. set over in the DU House and we were really excited. But it was radio. And a few disc jockeys were famous for playing jazz and I would tune in all the time to that. And what you see is the results.

Well I had thrown a few song names at Phil, like the stuff that was getting top 10 airplay in the fifties and you had things, even a Leroy Anderson song, “Blue Tango,” “How High the Moon” by Les Paul.
